localContext: Many Oak Lawn homes, especially the post-war brick ranches and Georgians from the 1950s and 60s, still use original garage door openers. problemSigns.sign: Opener hums but the door doesn't move
problemSigns.detail: This often indicates a stripped drive gear or a motor issue within the opener unit.

problemSigns.sign: Door reverses before touching the floor
problemSigns.detail: Safety sensors may be misaligned or obstructed. Travel limits might also need adjustment.
This can point to a logic board failure, a programming error, or dead batteries in the remote/keypad.
The blinking lights signal an obstruction, misalignment, or damage to the safety sensors.

problemSigns.sign: Trolley moves but door stays down
problemSigns.detail: This usually means a broken belt, chain, or a disconnected or damaged trolley carriage.
